chapter: Oliver, Kelly and the district bands
title: Drums, big dance halls and sailors' tips
summary: Drums were standard; Hunts and Nagle and the 101 Ranch drew Norwegian sailors whose tips included gold pieces.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Did, uh, was it a regular thing to have drums in the band?

Oh, practically most all the bands had drums. Oh, they did have drums? Yeah, that was the main instrument, a drum. Piano and drum, they always had that. Oh, did they? Yeah, they never did, they'd be without that drum. Oh. Out of all the time when they didn't have no blowing instruments, they used to have to have that drum, see.
What did they have, like a snare drum or... Regular, regular... Snare and bass?

Bass and snare drum, yeah, trap drum and bass drum, too, you see, yeah. And, uh, so from that on, after that, why, they, uh, the district, then they started to have all that blowing instruments, you see. And, uh, there was so much knowledge. You take Harry Parker, Harry Parker 101 Ranch, and, uh, uh, Hunts and Nagels, them was large places. Large dance halls. They had, they had women with, uh, what was employed there, just to sell a beer, you know. Big quarts of beer, and them, them chummies off the ships used to come through there, you know. Them Norwegian ships would come in port, and them fellas would come in, and, uh, that's the first place they'd go. One of them dance halls, and get in there and spend them on a drink and have a good time. They had a lot, a lot of time, we used to have our collection, Kitty Box, they called it. And, uh, we'd find ten dollar gold pieces in there instead of thinking. They was copper cents. These fellas would just go in their pocket and have all that change, you know. Gold money in it. And when we'd go to, and Maggie Mineta would tell you, when we'd go to whack up in the morning, we'd have ten dollar gold pieces in there. What they'd take for, for, uh, copper cents, you see.
Why do they call them chummies? Those are the sailors?

Yeah, sailors off the ships. Them time the ships would point into this port, you know, from the foreign ships, you know, coming in. Them Norwegian ships most so, they'd come in loaded down, you know. And the time they'd get in this, they'd pay off when they hit sea, you see. And them guys would be out of the sea, maybe, for three or four months like that, before they'd hear the port, you see. When they'd get here, they'd have plenty of money.
And they'd say, it was a good time then. Yeah.
